question: If voltage deterioration threatens to cause a voltage collapse, may a transmission operator tell the distribution grids and large users connected to it to switch off the automatic regulation of their transformers?
reply: {"gold_answers": "yes", "gold_reason": "Article 22(1)(c)(iv) lets a TSO instruct transmission-connected DSOs and significant grid users to block automatic voltage and reactive power control of transformers where voltage deterioration jeopardises operational security or threatens a voltage collapse. The reference answer quotes this correctly.", "other_articles": [{"doc_id": "reg_2017_1485_art23", "answers": "partially", "why": "Article 23(4) says affected transmission-connected SGUs and DSOs must execute TSO remedial-action instructions, but it does not mention blocking transformer control."}], "ambiguity": "none", "ambiguity_reason": "The question maps directly onto Article 22(1)(c)(iv).", "suggested_fix": ""}

verdict.gold_reason: Article 22(1)(c)(iv) lets a TSO instruct transmission-connected DSOs and significant grid users to block automatic voltage and reactive power control of transformers where voltage deterioration jeopardises operational security or threatens a voltage collapse. The reference answer quotes this correctly.

other_articles.why: Article 23(4) says affected transmission-connected SGUs and DSOs must execute TSO remedial-action instructions, but it does not mention blocking transformer control.

verdict.ambiguity_reason: The question maps directly onto Article 22(1)(c)(iv).
